title: Session Replay Redaction Playbook — Personal Notes
body:
Context
- Quick personal sketch for a small feature/ops playbook: make session replays (logs + transcripts + inputs/outputs) safe to store & share with engineers while preserving debugability.
- Goal: enable fast repro & root-cause without exposing PII, secrets, or customer-provided private data.
- Motivation: Support tickets and oncall debugging often require replaying a sequence of requests; currently teams either redaction-scrub (too aggressive, loses signal) or full-archive (privacy risk). Looking for middle ground: reversible-ish redaction for internal users + irreversible redaction for exported artifacts.

High-level constraints / guardrails
- Safety-first: default to redacted when uncertain. Anything classified as PHI/PII/credentials must be removed permanently for any asset that leaves the customer boundary.
- Developer ergonomics: replays must keep enough context to reproduce ordering, tokenization artifacts, and timing patterns.
- Auditability: record the redaction policy applied and who accessed the unredacted replay.
- Performance: redaction as a pipeline stage; should be able to run on live-sampled traffic or bulk export.

Use cases / user stories (prioritized)
1) Oncall developer needs to replay a failing chat session with full internal context to reproduce a bug. (S1)
   - Acceptance: developer can request unredacted replay via RBAC. Request logs audit event. Reconstructed replay includes original tokens but marks redacted spans.
2) CS engineer needs to share a sanitized transcript with a customer (irreversible redaction).
   - Acceptance: one-click sanitize export that permanently replaces redacted spans and removes metadata like IP/region.
3) Product manager wants to sample replays for quality evals but can't see PII.
   - Acceptance: sampling + automatic safe-redaction pipeline that preserves prompt structure and tokens counts.
4) Privacy compliance wants proofs of redaction (hashes + policy id) to show what was removed.
   - Acceptance: exported manifest with redaction diffs + policy version + checksums.

Redaction model ideas (multi-layer)
- Heuristic layer: regexes for emails, phone numbers, credit card numbers, social security patterns, JWT-looking strings.
- ML entity detection: lightweight NER tuned for user-supplied content (names, addresses, health terms). Model runs on text segments and returns confidence + span.
- Secret detectors / static patterns: API keys, org-specific tokens (pattern-based + allowlist).
- Tokenization-aware redaction: map redacted spans to token indices to avoid shifting context for replay rebuild.

Modes of redaction
- View-time masking: ephemeral masking in UI; underlying raw stored only accessible via elevated flow. For quick investigations.
- Stored-sanitized export: irreversible sanitize replacing chars with fixed markers ("[REDACTED_EMAIL]").
- Reversible vault: encrypted store where original content is stored encrypted with a key accessible to authorized roles (requires approval). Logs + TTL for decryption.

Developer tooling / UX notes
- Replay timeline UI should show redaction markers inline (hover reveals policy id, confidence).
- Breakpoints: allow stepping into request/response pairs; show token-level diff between original and sanitized for debugging.
- 'Reveal for debugging' flow: modal with justification, requestor, and approver; once approved, a temporary unredacted view is created with short TTL and audit log.
- CLI: small helper to fetch a replay bundle (sanitized by default) with flags --decrypt-if-approved and --purge-on-exit.

Data model sketch (flat fields only here)
- replay_id, sequence: array of events (timestamp, actor, token_indices, text_masked, text_hashed), redaction_policy_id, redaction_manifest_id.
- Keep a manifest per replay that records spans removed and salted hashes of removed content for later verification.

Acceptance / Evaluation plan
- Safety tests: create synthetic dataset with labeled PII and assert >= 99% removal for irreversible export and >= 95% for view-time masking (low false positives tolerated in irreversible exports only).
- Developer signal: A/B test two teams with and without token-index-preserving redaction; measure time-to-repro average.
- Latency/regressions: redaction pipeline should add < 50ms median to request archival (or be async).

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Reversible vs irreversible: who gets keys? How to manage legal requests? Might require enterprise-only gating.
- ML model FPs: Too many false positives will reduce debug signal. Need configurable thresholds per-team.
- Token index preservation: complex for multi-byte encodings and model tokenizers (BPE vs SentencePiece). Maybe store both raw char spans and token indices computed at ingest time.
- Cross-modal data: attachments/screenshots need separate redaction (OCR + image blur). Not addressing fully in MVP.

MVP proposal (6-week sprint)
- Phase 0 (week 0–1): define redaction policy schema, simple heuristics, manifest format, and RBAC flows.
- Phase 1 (week 2–4): implement pipeline that produces sanitized export + view-time masked UI. Include audit logs.
- Phase 2 (week 5–6): add reversible vault prototype + CLI fetch flow; wiring to approval modal.
- Deliverable: docs + demo + 1 oncall team pilot.

Quick TODOs (personal)
- [ ] Draft policy schema and sample manifest JSON (include hash salt strategy).
- [ ] Prototype token-index mapping for GPT2 BPE library.
- [ ] Wire simple regex redactors and run against 5k historical sessions for FP rate.
- [ ] Sketch approval modal and CLI UX.
- [ ] Sync with Legal + Compliance (Maya) re: reversible storage TTL and key custody.

Notes / ideas to park for later
- Differential privacy-style aggregates for QA dashboards (instead of raw replays).
- Shareable ephemeral links that auto-expire and revoke access.
- Integration with Redwood Optimize: redaction-aware eval suites that only compare non-sensitive tokens.

Unresolved: what counts as "sensitive enough" to banish from any internal unredacted view? Need a list + legal input.

End of notes.
